svg.aria-label: Figure 1.6: The Salt Trap and 700-Year Decline of Wheat in Southern Mesopotamian Temple Records
svg.text: Figure 1.6: The Salt Trap — Why Wheat Vanished From Southern Cities
Trapped basin drainage and 45°C summer heat drew mineral salt into topsoil, tracked across 700 years of temple tablets
A. How Fierce Summer Sun Salted Low Fields
Cross-section of a low-lying southern Mesopotamian basin

g.text: Low-lying basin has poor drainage, so excess water cannot flow away

svg.text: B. Wheat's Share of Southern Grain Harvests
Tracked in southern temple clay tablets (c. 2400–1700 BCE)
Remaining grain harvest shifted to salt-tolerant barley
As rising soil salt cut wheat harvests across southern cities,
grain power and political control shifted north to Babylon.
